title: A queue, its storage and its workers
question: What changes when an event leaves the queue, and what does not?

steps.title: Waiting order is visible
steps.narration: An authored state snapshot shows three waiting events. Arrival order is a property of this scenario, not evidence of all distributed producers.

steps.title: Removing the first list element shifts the remainder
steps.narration: Python list pop(0) incurs O(n) movement. No milliseconds or speed ratio are inferred from that asymptotic statement.

steps.title: A different data structure serves the same interface
steps.narration: deque provides approximately O(1) append/pop at its ends. This is a local data-structure choice, not durable message storage.
steps.takeaway: Use measured workload evidence before claiming a performance gain.

steps.title: Dequeued is not completed or acknowledged
steps.narration: A worker may fail after dequeue. Multiple workers can complete out of order. A durable broker, bounded queue, acknowledgement, dead-letter policy and backpressure are separate design choices.
questions: What happens when producers outrun consumers?
Is task_done only accounting, or a durable acknowledgement?
